method: Every field is validated before any text is produced. The interface name is limited to 15 characters chosen from letters, digits, dot, underscore, colon, at sign and hyphen, the Linux limit on interface name length, and the file priority must be a whole number from 1 to 99 written as a two-digit prefix. Static mode accepts 1 to 16 IPv4 addresses written as address/prefix; each octet must be a decimal 0 to 255 without a leading zero, the prefix must be 0 to 32, and a repeated address is refused. For each address the block size is 2^(32-prefix), the network address is the address rounded down to a multiple of that size, and the broadcast address is the last address in the block; the usable count is size minus two for prefixes up to 30, two for a /31 and one for a /32, and the usable first and last addresses follow from those boundaries and are shown in a table. A gateway must be a plain IPv4 address, and it is flagged when it falls outside every configured block, when it lands on a network or broadcast address, or when it sits inside a /31 or /32 range. At most four IPv4 DNS servers and eight search domains are accepted; domains are checked label by label and limited to 253 characters, and they are lowercased. MTU is optional, an integer from 576 to 9000, and a value below the IPv6 minimum of 1280 is reported. DHCP mode writes DHCP=ipv4, ipv6 or yes with matching [DHCPv4] and [DHCPv6] sections carrying UseDNS and UseDomains; static mode writes DHCP=no, one Address line per entry, and optional Gateway, DNS, Domains, IPv6AcceptRA and MTU lines. The file opens with a comment naming its install path. The output is text only: the page cannot inspect the host, choose an interface name for you or reload systemd-networkd, and it does not model policy routing, bridges, VLANs or IPv6 addresses.
